definition: Idiom for a woman who is sexually promiscuous and emotionally fickle; literally 'having the nature of water and willow catkins,' both of which drift without anchorage.
notes: Always gendered female; the natural metaphor frames sexual looseness as moral weightlessness rather than explicit conduct.

definition: 'A beautiful face is water that brings calamity'; idiom attributing disaster to female attractiveness, blaming women for the downfall of men who desired them.
notes: No English equivalent captures both the beauty-as-weapon framing and the explicit blame-displacement onto women for male downfall; used to excuse male failures from historical emperors to modern men.

definition: Idiom condemning a group as utterly morally bankrupt; literally 'the men are thieves and the women are prostitutes,' applying the worst gendered moral failure to each sex simultaneously.
notes: The prostitution accusation (女娼) is the more damaging half in Confucian moral framing; the compound insult targets couples, families, or political factions.

definition: 'Green hat'; the canonical Chinese symbol for cuckoldry — a man said to be wearing a green hat has been sexually betrayed by his wife or partner.
notes: Green as the cuckold color derives from Yuan/Ming dynasty sumptuary law requiring male relatives of prostitutes to wear green headgear; now ubiquitous in internet memes and everyday idiom.

definition: 'Rotten goods'; a crude misogynistic slur for a sexually promiscuous woman, framing her body as spoiled merchandise.
notes: The commodity metaphor (货 = goods/merchandise) is central, treating female sexual value as a physical asset depleted by use; also applied as a general insult for any morally debased person.

definition: 'Integrity and shame'; the Confucian virtue of having an appropriate capacity for moral shame, especially regarding sexual conduct; most commonly invoked negatively (没有廉耻) to accuse someone of brazen indecency.
notes: English has no equivalent for the positive value of feeling sexual shame appropriately; Chinese moral philosophy treats this capacity as a prerequisite for ethical personhood, not an inhibition to overcome.

definition: 'Shameless'; brazenly lacking any sense of moral shame, especially regarding sexual conduct or social propriety.
notes: Applicable across all moral domains; in sexual contexts specifically targets conduct that openly violates norms of modesty without remorse.

definition: 'Shame'; the subjective experience of sexual or moral shame, especially regarding conduct that violates social norms of modesty or chastity.
notes: Captures the internal emotional dimension of Confucian shame culture; distinct from 耻辱, which emphasizes external social disgrace; the concept bridges personal guilt and communal accountability.

definition: 'Disgrace and humiliation'; the state of being publicly shamed for sexual misconduct, encompassing the social condemnation and the loss of standing it produces.
notes: More externally oriented than 羞耻; implies visible social consequences and witnesses; commonly the outcome of the community's moral condemnation of sexual behavior deemed improper.

definition: 'Unchaste'; the state of being sexually unfaithful or impure, especially applied to women who have violated expectations of marital or pre-marital chastity.
notes: Inherently gendered — chastity (贞) is coded as a female virtue in traditional Chinese morality, so its negation almost always indicts women; rarely applied to men.

definition: 'Lewdly disordered'; extreme sexual promiscuity or moral disorder, implying that unrestrained lust has corrupted one's character and social life.
notes: 淫 alone signals sexual excess; 乱 (disorder/chaos) amplifies this to systemic moral breakdown; used in legal and official contexts for sexual misconduct serious enough to warrant punishment.

definition: 'Improper conduct and character'; a formal accusation of moral character defects encompassing sexual misconduct, dishonesty, and violations of social virtue.
notes: Functions as a bureaucratic condemnation in workplace, school, and legal contexts; sexual misconduct is among the most common specific triggers in Chinese institutional settings.

definition: 'Damaging customs and corrupting public morals'; a formal condemnation of behavior — typically sexual — judged to undermine community values and social order.
notes: Used in legal, media, and official contexts to justify censorship and punishment of sexual content or behavior; the concept directly underpins Chinese obscenity law enforcement.

definition: 'Disgracing the family tradition'; to bring shame upon the entire family lineage through sexual misconduct, treating the family's moral reputation as a multigenerational asset that can be damaged.
notes: The concept of 门风 (family tradition/wind) is specifically Chinese — sexual misconduct reflects not just on the individual but dishonors the lineage across generations; no English equivalent captures this collectivist multigenerational shame structure.

definition: 'Privately born child'; an illegitimate child born outside of marriage, carrying the social stigma of its parents' unsanctioned sexual union.
notes: More neutral in register than 野种; in contemporary usage appears in legal, journalistic, or clinical contexts; associated stigma has diminished in urban China but persists in more traditional communities.

definition: 'Wild breed'; a crude contemptuous slur for an illegitimate child, framing the child as biologically and morally inferior due to being born outside of marriage.
notes: Significantly cruder and more dehumanizing than 私生子; the 野 (wild, uncivilized) component implies a perceived hereditary moral taint alongside the illegitimacy.

definition: 'The fondness of the cut sleeve'; a classical literary allusion to male homosexuality, from Emperor Ai of Han (r. 7–1 BCE) who cut his sleeve rather than disturb his sleeping male favorite, Dong Xian.
notes: Most widely recognized of the Chinese classical allusions to homosexuality; 断袖 alone suffices as a shorthand in literary contexts; the low crude score reflects its elegant literary framing.

definition: 'The preference of Lord Longyang'; a classical allusion to male homosexual love from the Warring States period (c. 3rd century BCE), involving Lord Longyang and the King of Wei.
notes: Less recognized than 断袖之癖 among general audiences; 龙阳 alone functions as a classical shorthand for a gay man; standard in scholarly and historical discussions of pre-modern Chinese sexuality.

definition: 'Half-eaten peach'; a classical allusion to male homosexual affection, from Mizi Xia sharing a half-eaten peach with Duke Linggong of Wei as an expression of love.
notes: Among the more obscure of the classical allusions in modern awareness; typically appears paired with 断袖 in the compound 分桃断袖; conveys the tenderness of male love more than its sexual dimension.

definition: 'Sharing the peach, cutting the sleeve'; a compound classical allusion combining the two most famous Chinese literary symbols of male same-sex love (余桃 and 断袖) into a single idiom.
notes: More recognizable than 余桃 alone; used in scholarly, literary, and increasingly in historical fiction and danmei (男男 romance) contexts to signal male same-sex desire with classical gravitas.

definition: 'Male custom'; a Ming dynasty term for male homosexuality, referring to the practice as a social phenomenon (风, custom/wind) rather than framing it clinically or morally.
notes: Homophone of 南风 (nánfēng, 'southern wind') but uses 男 (male) rather than 南 (south); more historically descriptive while 南风 is more euphemistic; both refer to male same-sex practice.

definition: 'Rabbit deity'; in its historical sexual sense, a term for young male sex workers in imperial Beijing who served male clients; distinct from its modern identity as a beloved Beijing folk-art clay figure.
notes: The word today overwhelmingly evokes the endearing Mid-Autumn Festival clay rabbit deity; the historical sexual meaning is largely unknown outside historical scholarship; recognition score reflects awareness of the sexual meaning only, not the folk figure.

definition: Historically, young male Peking opera performers who supplemented their income through sexual services to male patrons; the same word now means 'mister' or, in some dialects, a wife's affectionate term for her husband.
notes: The sexual meaning (male theatrical prostitute) is archaic and unrecognized by most modern speakers; in the Qing dynasty, 相公 houses were the male equivalent of brothels; recognition score reflects the historical sexual meaning, not the word's dominant modern meanings.

definition: 'Beautiful/graceful boy'; a boy kept for sexual use by an adult male patron; the Chinese equivalent of the Latin catamite, describing the historical institution of powerful men maintaining young male sexual servants.
notes: Distinct from modern clinical concepts (pedophilia/ephebophilia) in describing a historically normalized social institution with economic and social dimensions; appeared in legal codes, poetry, and social commentary throughout Chinese history.

definition: 'Southern wind'; a classical euphemism for male homosexuality, possibly referencing regions of China where it was considered more socially prevalent.
notes: Exact homophone of 男风 (nánfēng, 'male custom') using 南 (south) rather than 男 (male); the sexual meaning is almost entirely archaic and unrecognized by modern speakers without literary training; recognition score reflects awareness of the historical sexual meaning only.
